title: Micron Stock Has Gained Roughly 190% in 2026. History Says Its Next 30%+ Drawdown Could Come at Any Time.
author: Leo Sun
description: Micron's stock has surged nearly 190% in 2026 driven by AI-driven demand for memory chips. However, the company's historical pattern of boom-and-bust cycles in the memory market suggests a 30%+ drawdown could occur soon, despite strong growth projections through 2028. Analysts tend to overestimate growth during hot markets and underestimate during downturns, making volatility inevitable.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the article acknowledges Micron's strong 190% gain in 2026 and its well-positioned role in the AI boom with impressive growth projections, it emphasizes significant historical volatility and the high probability of a 30%+ drawdown in the near term. The neutral sentiment reflects both bullish fundamentals and bearish technical/cyclical risks.

title: Prediction: 3 Unstoppable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That Will Join the $2 Trillion Club by 2027 (Hint: Not SpaceX)
author: Keithen Drury
description: An analyst predicts that Broadcom, Micron, and Meta Platforms will each reach $2 trillion market valuations by 2027. Broadcom is positioned to cross $2 trillion by end of 2026 driven by custom AI chip demand with expected $100B+ AI semiconductor revenue in 2027. Micron, currently at $940B valuation, could double based on strong memory chip demand and projected 84% revenue growth. Meta, at $1.5T, is expected to surge as its advertising business benefits from AI tools and potential cloud computing expansion.

title: Sandisk Trades at 43 Times Earnings and 7 Times Next Year's Earnings Estimates. What Has to Go Right for the Cheap Number to Win?
author: Daniel Sparks
description: Sandisk stock fell sharply (22.8% over two days) amid broader memory chip sector selloff. The stock presents a valuation puzzle: trading at 43x trailing earnings but only 7x forward earnings. This disconnect reflects the company's dramatic recovery from losses a year ago to $23 per share earnings as AI-driven NAND flash demand surged. The cheap forward multiple assumes earnings will continue climbing well beyond management's guidance, requiring sustained NAND price increases into 2027. While the company has secured multi-year supply agreements and maintains zero debt, the valuation carries significant cycle risk.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents a balanced view of Sandisk's investment case. While the company shows strong operational recovery with gross margins reaching 78.4% and data center revenue surging 651% year-over-year, the stock faces significant valuation risk. The 46% decline from its peak and the disconnect between trailing (43x) and forward (7x) multiples suggest the market is pricing in substantial cycle risk. The neutral sentiment reflects both the bullish fundamentals (multi-year contracts, zero debt) and bearish concerns (memory pricing cyclicality, earnings sustainability).

title: Why Sandisk Stock Keeps Crashing
author: Rich Smith
description: Sandisk stock has plummeted 31% in three days due to two main concerns: Chinese chipmaker CXMT's $487 billion IPO raising $8 billion threatens to disrupt memory chip markets and erode Sandisk's high profit margins through competitive pricing, and broader investor worries about potential cuts to AI infrastructure spending that could reduce demand for memory chips.

title: MEXC Users Put Nearly a Third of First-Month RealStocks Volume Into SpaceX
author: Mexc
description: MEXC's RealStocks platform, which launched June 1st offering access to 7,000+ US stocks and ETFs, reported strong first-month trading insights. SpaceX dominated with 29.70% of trading volume, while seven AI-related assets collectively captured 23.67% of volume. The platform attracted over 120,000 users in its first month, with more than 40% of volume distributed outside the top 10 holdings, indicating portfolio-building behavior rather than speculative trading.
